# Indriyakathā (Ps 1.4)

**ID:** Ps 1.4

**Title (Pali):** Indriyakathā

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Indriyakathā* ("Discussion of Faculties") is the fourth treatise (*kathā*) in the first division (*Mahāvagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Gethin 2001]. Unlike comprehensive Abhidhamma treatments that analyze the full list of twenty-two faculties, the *Indriyakathā* concerns itself exclusively with the five spiritual faculties (*indriya*): faith (*saddhā*), energy (*viriya*), mindfulness (*sati*), concentration (*samādhi*), and wisdom (*paññā*) [Gethin 2001]. In its exposition of their controlling functions, the text explains how each faculty brings its specific opposite under control: faith controls lack of confidence or faithlessness, energy controls indolence, mindfulness controls heedlessness, concentration controls agitation, and wisdom controls ignorance [Nyanaponika 1976]. At its conclusion, the exposition integrates all seven constituent sets of the thirty-seven *bodhipakkhiyā dhammā* [Gethin 2001].
